hypothesis: On a T4 (sm_75) the CUDA chain's prompt attention is cc_attn_fk, two passes over the keys, because cc_attn_f2 (one pass, online softmax, mma.sync m16n8k16) needs sm_80. Each m16n8k16 is two m16n8k8 with the same fragments, and at head dim 256 blocks of 16 keys fit the T4's 64 KiB of shared memory: one pass then reads a long prompt faster.
command: bench.c built against c/ (make CUDA=1 CUDA_ARCH=sm_75, as bench build does); COLI_CUDA=1 COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=auto OMP_WAIT_POLICY=ACTIVE OMP_PROC_BIND=close ./qwen36-bench --model <model> --text promessi_sposi.txt --lengths 2048,3072,4096,5120,6144,7168,8192 --gen 128 --teacher

hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.00GHz (4 cores / 8 threads, 38.5 MiB L3) + NVIDIA Tesla T4 (15360 MiB, sm_75, up to PCIe Gen3 x16)
hardware.storage: Google Colab VM disk (the model downloaded to /content before the runs)
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Google Colab, T4 high-RAM), CUDA 13.0 (nvcc V13.0.88), driver 580.82.07, gcc 13.3.0

config.scenario: the 8192-token prompt of the ladder up (2048, 3072, ... 8192 in one process, each followed by 128 teacher-forced words)
config.tok_s: prompt tokens / the prompt's seconds (bench's prefill_tps of the 8192 row)

quality.method: make -C c check (macOS arm64); on the T4, make -C c cuda-chain-check and make -C c cuda-test pass, and the chain's prompt rows fail against the reference with either m16n8k8 pair mutated (correctness.txt). The logits change, as cc_attn_f2's own comment says against cc_attn_fk (one pass sums in another order): every run of a version here has the same 8192-token fingerprint (a 6f65ef58272e05ec, b 5e5537ed77c416aa); over 1024 teacher-forced words after an 8192-token prompt b's nll is +0.12% (standard error 0.10%) and its top-1 0.3 points lower (standard error 0.3) (quality.txt)
